newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua's Aleman calls for calm as strike nears.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua's Aleman calls for calm as strike nears.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman called on Friday for calm as tensions grew around a planned national strike by left-wing Sandinista unions and grassroots groups against the government's economic policy.

"I hope that the hot heads have been left behind. These disturbances and destabilisations only hurt Nicaragua," Aleman told reporters after meeting with conservative Cardinal Miguel Obando y Bravo, one of Nicaragua's most powerful figures.
Aleman said he asked Obando y Bravo to include a call for peace and reconciliation in his usual Sunday homily, the day before the planned protest.
"I hope it will be a civic protest on Monday and that we Nicaraguans have our heads well centred on our shoulders," the conservative Obando y Bravo said.

Sandinista unions and farmer organisations are angered by what they see as the "dictatorial attitude" of Aleman's government and have called for changes in its economic austerity programme, which they say is throwing people out of work and pushing the country deeper into poverty.

Planned actions include strikes by transportation and state workers unions, protest marches and the blockage of highways to paralyse traffic, Daniel Nunez, president of the pro-Sandinista National Union of Farmers and Ranchers, told Reuters.
Aleman's call for calm came after the head of Nicaragua's Central Bank and business leaders warned the protest could threaten Nicaragua's economic growth and stability.
